Q: Case labels only if global variables exist A:

You have the right of it, Niko. #if defined is no better at detecting global variables than #ifdef. Example: https://godbolt.org/z/f5GjWrefa . This is because the preprocessor executes before the compiler comes along and figures out what is and isn't a variable.

Q: Confusion about Price range A:

Estimate the total hours for design, development, testing, meetings, revisions, and deployment. Then decide an hourly value based on your skills and project complexity. Price the project from the value of your time and effort, not from your student status.

Q: How to Schedule Weekly Asyncio Tasks A:

Also see Python Asyncio schedule tasks weekly. asyncio is mostly intended to run I/O-bound units of work without blocking each other. I'd use your system cron daemon to kick off scheduled tasks like this.

Q: What do you use to keep track of everything? A:

  1. Create a Master Sites Database. Every task you ever do is "Linked" to a site in that database.

  2. You can click on "Client A," see their 3 websites, click on "Website 1," and see every password, every maintenance log, and every historical task in one view.

  3. If using these for passwords, ensure you use a dedicated vault (like Bitwarden or 1Password) and only link the vault URL in the database rather than storing plain-text passwords.

Q: Converting several video files into audio with MoviePy A:

from moviepy.editor import VideoFileClip, AudioFileClip

import subprocess

input_video = "/mnt/data/1869.mp4"

output_video = "/mnt/data/video_sin_voz.mp4"

temp_audio = "/mnt/data/temp_audio.wav"

karaoke_audio = "/mnt/data/karaoke_audio.wav"

# Extraer audio

clip = VideoFileClip(input_video)

clip.audio.write_audiofile(temp_audio, fps=44100, nbytes=2, codec="pcm_s16le", logger=None)

# Remover voz aproximada

subprocess.run([

"ffmpeg", "-y", 

"-i", temp_audio, 

"-af", "pan=stereo|c0=c0-c1|c1=c1-c0", 

karaoke_audio

], check=True)

# Crear video final

new_audio = AudioFileClip(karaoke_audio)

final_clip = clip.set_audio(new_audio)

final_clip.write_videofile(output_video, codec="libx264", audio_codec="aac", logger=None)
